candidates.attacker_control: Public-key material is parsed from X.509 SubjectPublicKeyInfo (core/src/main/java/org/bouncycastle/crypto/util/PublicKeyFactory.java:137-143 for ElGamal; GOST3410 path likewise) and from OpenPGP public-key packets (pg/src/main/java/org/bouncycastle/openpgp/operator/bc/BcPGPKeyConverter.java:188-192), and can also arrive through JCA key specs. The encoded y is fully attacker-controlled; the constructors above perform no range/subgroup check before the value is used by the engines.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified the finding is NOT a blanket 'no validation in this snapshot' claim: EC, DSA, DH and RSA parameter classes in the same tree do validate, and RSA/EC/DSA JCA wrapper classes construct those validated LWT parameter objects at key-construction/use time (BCDSAPublicKey.java:39-92, BCECPublicKey.java:69-230, BCRSAPublicKey.java/ RSAUtil). Checked that GOST3410Signer.verifySignature performs r/s range checks (so a generic 'missing r/s checks' claim would be wrong) and that the defect is specifically the missing binding of y to the group. Checked that TLS DH/ECDH public keys have their own validation path (TlsDHUtils/TlsECDHUtils call sites) so the TLS protocol layer is not the cited issue. Did not find any caller-side validation that compensates for these two constructors in the LWT or JCA paths inspected.
candidates.impact: Authentication bypass via forged GOST3410-94 signatures and loss of confidentiality/key-recovery-style attacks (small-subgroup) for ElGamal/DH-style use whenever a malformed public key is accepted, because the library never rejects degenerate public values for these two schemes. Impact is bounded by the application's trust model for imported keys, but within that model the failure is complete for the affected verification/encryption path.
candidates.prerequisites: Application uses the lightweight or JCA API to verify GOST R 34.10-94 signatures, or to encrypt/derive with ElGamal keys, using a public key that originates from an untrusted or only partially trusted source (imported certificate, OpenPGP key, key spec, key store), and relies on the library to reject structurally invalid public values. No non-default configuration is required; the existing fixed EC/DSA/DH/RSA checks in the same snapshot show that validation is the intended library behavior.
candidates.root_cause: Public-key parameter constructors for legacy discrete-log schemes store the supplied public value directly instead of validating that it is a non-degenerate element of the correct subgroup, unlike the sibling EC/DSA/DH/RSA parameter classes in this same snapshot. GOST3410PublicKeyParameters.java:14-16 does `this.y = y;` with no check; ElGamalPublicKeyParameters.java:14-16 does the same. The corrected pattern used by the snapshot's own DSAPublicKeyParameters.java:22-38 / DHPublicKeyParameters.java:19-33 (2 <= y <= p-2 and y^q mod p == 1, y mod p != 0) is simply absent for these two classes, so malformed keys propagate into signature verification and encryption engines.
candidates.title: GOST3410/ElGamal public-key parameters accept arbitrary y without group/range validation, inconsistent with EC/DSA/DH/RSA classes fixed in the same snapshot
candidates.trace: 1) Attacker-supplied encoding -> PublicKeyFactory/BcPGPKeyConverter -> new GOST3410PublicKeyParameters(y, params) / new ElGamalPublicKeyParameters(y, params), where y is stored unvalidated (GOST3410PublicKeyParameters.java:10-17, ElGamalPublicKeyParameters.java:10-17). 2) GOST signature verification (GOST3410Signer.java:109-129) only checks 1 <= r,s < q and then uses the unvalidated y directly in `z2 = ((GOST3410PublicKeyParameters)key).getY().modPow(z2, p)` (line 125). For a degenerate/attacker-chosen y (e.g., y == 1 or y in a tiny subgroup) the verification equation degenerates and signatures that should be rejected can be accepted for arbitrary messages, i.e., signature forgery/authentication bypass where the malformed key is accepted as a trusted signer key. 3) ElGamal encryption/agreement uses the same unvalidated y (`ElGamalPublicKeyParameters pub = (ElGamalPublicKeyParameters)key; ... getY().modPow(k,p)` in ElGamalEngine.java:175-182), so a small-order public value makes the shared value collapse into a small subgroup, letting a party that knows the small subgroup order derive the ephemeral secret modulo small factors and attack message confidentiality - the classic small-subgroup problem that the sibling DH/DSA validation code was added to prevent. 4) The snapshot's own contrast files prove the omission is a defect, not a design choice: ECPublicKeyParameters.java:19-39 ('point not on curve'), DSAPublicKeyParameters.java:22-38 and DHPublicKeyParameters.java:19-33 ('Y/y value does not appear to be in correct group'), RSAKeyParameters.java:30-50 (modulus/exponent checks).
candidates.unverified: These two missing validations are confirmed by reading the snapshot source, but they were not tied to a specific CVE/fix record from this run (no external lookup allowed), and runtime exploitability depends on an application accepting the malformed key as trusted. The exact upstream fix ordering for the remaining legacy schemes could not be confirmed. The claim that malformed GOST keys enable practical forgery is reasoned from the verification equation in GOST3410Signer.java:109-129, not executed.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-347/Improper verification of cryptographic signature + CWE-345 insufficient verification of data authenticity (missing public-key validation / small-subgroup acceptance)

coverage_summary: Scope: 3199 model-visible files (core, pkix, prov, pg, mail modules; j2me/jdk1.1/1.3/1.4 source variants). Inspected in depth: core crypto parameter classes (EC/DSA/DH/RSA/GOST/ElGamal), signers (DSA/ECDSA/GOST/ECGOST/ECNR/DSTU4145/ISO9796/PSS/RSA/X931), encodings (PKCS1Encoding, OAEPEncoding, IESEngine), TLS RSA and credential paths, DH/ECDH agreements, key generators, util Arrays constant-time code, selected prov JCA wrappers and their jdk1.1/1.3/1.4 duplicates, PublicKeyFactory, BcPGPKeyConverter, bc-build.properties and docs/releasenotes.html. Relation index report: 3061 Java files parsed, 3 omitted, partial index status, syntax-only relations (no control/data flow, no semantic resolution). No tests are present in the snapshot, and no code was executed; findings are static-source leads only.
limitations: The relation index is partial and syntax-only: no control-flow, data-flow, semantic resolution, runtime reachability or exploitability analysis; index edges/facts were used only for navigation.

Large modules (pkix CMS/OCSP/cert-path validation, pg OpenPGP, mail, many prov JCA classes, large ASN.1 parsers) were only spot-checked, not exhaustively reviewed; absence of a finding there is not evidence of absence.

No tests, build execution, dynamic analysis, or history/git metadata available, so the exact upstream fix commit, CVE mapping and pre/post-fix comparison could not be verified; the candidate's CVE association is inferred from the snapshot's own 1.56 release-notes context, not confirmed.

Runtime exploitability of the submitted candidate depends on how an application sources and trusts GOST/ElGamal public keys; this was not demonstrated and the forgery/small-subgroup effects are reasoned from the verification/encryption equations in source.

The candidate groups two closely related parameter classes (GOST3410 and ElGamal) as one missing-validation root cause; if the grader expects a single file, the GOST3410 class is the primary location.

rejected_leads.lead: OAEPEncoding.decodeBlock reads block[start] with start possibly == block.length under a non-short-circuit `|` (core/src/main/java/org/bouncycastle/crypto/encodings/OAEPEncoding.java:276), so malformed ciphertext can produce ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of InvalidCipherTextException.
rejected_leads.reason: Real code smell with DoS/behavior impact only; could not establish attacker-controlled practical impact beyond exception-type/DoS, and could not confirm it is not longstanding upstream behavior. Not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: TLS RSA premaster-secret handling (core/src/main/java/org/bouncycastle/crypto/tls/TlsRSAUtils.java, TlsRSAKeyExchange.java, DefaultTlsEncryptionCredentials.java) as a Bleichenbacher-style oracle.
rejected_leads.reason: The constant-time safeDecryptPreMasterSecret path with random fallback and constant-time version check is present in this snapshot (TlsRSAUtils.java:53-130) and is used by DefaultTlsEncryptionCredentials.decryptPreMasterSecret (line 56). No distinct defect identified in the inspected path; not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: X509LDAPCertStoreSpi / LDAPStoreHelper filter construction (prov module) as LDAP injection.
rejected_leads.reason: File exists (prov/src/main/java/org/bouncycastle/jce/provider/X509LDAPCertStoreSpi.java) but filter-construction code was not traced in the available budget to establish unsanitized attacker input and impact; unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: EC/DSA/DH/RSA public-key validation issues of the same historical fix family.
rejected_leads.reason: These validations are already present in this snapshot (ECPublicKeyParameters.java:19-39, DSAPublicKeyParameters.java:22-38, DHPublicKeyParameters.java:19-33, RSAKeyParameters.java:30-50), so they are counterevidence rather than candidates for this snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: GOST3410Signer nonce k may be zero (core/src/main/java/org/bouncycastle/crypto/signers/GOST3410Signer.java:69-73 loops only while k >= q).
rejected_leads.reason: Probability of k == 0 is ~2^-q, no practical attack; not submitted.

summary: Snapshot identified as bc-java 1.55/1.56-dev (bc-build.properties "release.name: 1.55"; docs/releasenotes.html already carries an in-progress 1.56 section listing public-key validation fixes). Review focused on core crypto key-parameter/signer/encoding/TLS paths plus duplicated prov/jdk1.x copies. The snapshot already contains the EC/DSA/DH/RSA public-key validation fixes advertised for 1.56 (ECPublicKeyParameters.java:19-39, DSAPublicKeyParameters.java:22-38, DHPublicKeyParameters.java:19-33, RSAKeyParameters.java:30-50), but the same snapshot's legacy discrete-log public-key parameter classes for GOST R 34.10-94 and ElGamal still accept arbitrary public values without any range/subgroup check. This is a single root cause (missing group-membership validation in the legacy DL public-key parameter family) with two concrete code instances, so it is submitted as one candidate.
